newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Daiwa replaces Nomura in Israel samurai issue.
newsitem.headline: Daiwa replaces Nomura in Israel samurai issue.

text.p: Israel has named Daiwa Securities as lead manager in place of Nomura Securities for the samurai issue now rescheduled to take place in the third quarter, Israel's Treasury said on Thursday.

"In light of recent developments in the (Nomura criminal) investigation it is clear that the government of Israel could not ensure the successful completion of the issue with Nomura as lead manager during 1997," Treasury accountant-general Shy Talmon said in a statement.

The issue, which is expected to raise 15 billion to 20 billion yen, was originally scheduled to take place in early June before Japan's securities watchdog opened an investigation into allegations that Nomura had illegal dealings with corporate racketeers.
In May, Talmon said that because of the investigation Israel was postponing the issue indefinitely.

The Treasury, however, is determined to go through with the samurai issue this year as part of a programme to test international debt markets before U.S. loan guarantees expire at the end of next year.
Talmon said completing the issue, its first ever in the Japanese market, by the end of the year was a key part of the programme. He added that Nomura had consented to the change.
Daiwa was one of seven investment banks chosen to underwrite the samurai issue and was a senior manager.
